source: Deb, Pratap, Agarwal, Meyarivan (2002) A fast and elitist multiobjective genetic algorithm: NSGA-II
finding: Founding computational model for trade-off search. Fixes three faults of the first NSGA: slow sorting, no elitism, a sharing parameter. Parents and children are merged, ranked by non-domination front, ties broken by crowding distance.
numbers: Fast non-dominated sort costs O(MN^2) (M objectives, N population); the old NSGA cost O(MN^3). Elitism by merging parent and offspring populations.
quote: is able to find much better spread of solutions and better convergence near the true Pareto-optimal front
limits: Ranking is in objective space only. Crowding distance is a cheap spread estimate, exact only in 2 objectives.
agent_relevance: S7 select can be done by code: rank candidates by dominance, then keep the diverse ones. No model judgement needed. Matches G5.

source: Deb, Pratap, Agarwal, Meyarivan (2002) A fast and elitist multiobjective genetic algorithm: NSGA-II
finding: Test design on nine problems: SCH, FON, POL, KUR and ZDT1-4,6. All algorithms got the same evaluation budget; NSGA-II was compared with PAES and SPEA.
numbers: Maximum 25,000 function evaluations for all. NSGA-II 250 generations at population 100. PAES archive 100. SPEA population 80 plus external 20. Ten runs each for mean and variance.
limits: Synthetic problems, mostly 2 objectives. Only 10 runs. Budget counted in evaluations, not wall time.
agent_relevance: Shows the right way to compare selectors: equal budget, repeated runs, both convergence and diversity measured. Matches G7.

source: Deb, Pratap, Agarwal, Meyarivan (2002) A fast and elitist multiobjective genetic algorithm: NSGA-II
finding: Result: NSGA-II converges better than PAES and SPEA in all problems except ZDT3 and ZDT6 (PAES better there), and has the best diversity on all nine problems.
numbers: Convergence: NSGA-II best in 7 of 9 problems, PAES better in 2 of 9. Diversity: NSGA-II best in 9 of 9. Worst diversity: PAES. On ZDT6 SPEA converged better than NSGA-II.
limits: Metrics are the authors' own convergence and spread measures.
agent_relevance: A selector can win on spread yet lose on convergence. Track coverage of options and closeness to best, not one score.

source: Deb, Pratap, Agarwal, Meyarivan (2002) A fast and elitist multiobjective genetic algorithm: NSGA-II
finding: Boundary condition: ZDT4 has 21^9 (about 7.94e11) local Pareto-optimal fronts. At population 100 NSGA-II and PAES both got stuck on local fronts, but NSGA-II kept a good spread. Binary-coded NSGA-II struggled to converge.
numbers: ZDT4: 7.94 x 10^11 local fronts, one global. Distance between consecutive local sets is 0.25 in decision space. Running 500 instead of 250 generations improved POL, KUR, ZDT3, ZDT4, ZDT6 (Table IV).
limits: Authors say no multiobjective GA of this size is expected to find the global front on ZDT4.
agent_relevance: Local optima apply to trade-off search too. A stable candidate set is not proof the true set was found (G3).

source: Deb, Pratap, Agarwal, Meyarivan (2002) A fast and elitist multiobjective genetic algorithm: NSGA-II
finding: Constraint handling: the dominance definition is changed so a feasible solution always beats an infeasible one, and among infeasible ones the smaller violation wins. Tested on constrained problems including a five-objective, seven-constraint nonlinear problem.
numbers: No penalty weights needed. Compared with another constrained multiobjective optimizer; NSGA-II reported much better.
limits: The five-objective problem is a single case; no significance test in the section read.
agent_relevance: Constraints first, then trade-offs: filter infeasible options by code before ranking. Clean rule for S7.

source: Guerreiro, Fonseca (2020) The Hypervolume Indicator: Problems and Algorithms
finding: Hypervolume is the most used set-quality indicator. It is strictly monotone with respect to set dominance, still unique to hypervolume-based indicators. One number covers closeness, spread and diversity.
numbers: 2D hypervolume in O(n log n). 3D has an O(n log n) algorithm (HVDC3D). Hypervolume contribution problems are #P-hard. Subset selection is NP-hard for d>=3. Overmars-Yap algorithm O(n^(d/2) log n).
quote: its theoretical properties justify its wide acceptance, particularly the strict monotonicity with respect to set dominance
limits: Depends on the chosen reference point. Cost explodes with number of objectives.
agent_relevance: A cheap code-computed scalar for 'how good is this option set'. Good for a budget stop rule, not a model opinion.

source: Guerreiro, Fonseca (2020) The Hypervolume Indicator: Problems and Algorithms
finding: The review states the decision-maker problem: no single optimum exists, the best choice depends on subjective preference, so under no preference an optimizer should deliver a finite representative subset of the Pareto front.
numbers: Quality of a point set is judged on closeness to the front, even distribution and spread.
limits: The pick-one step lies outside the optimizer. Hypervolume bakes in preference through the reference point.
agent_relevance: Separate 'produce the non-dominated set' (code) from 'pick one' (needs the user's stated priorities). Do not let the model invent weights.

source: Daulton, Balandat, Bakshy (2020) Differentiable Expected Hypervolume Improvement for Parallel Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization
finding: qEHVI: exact (up to Monte Carlo error) joint expected hypervolume improvement for a batch of q candidates, with exact gradients by autodiff. Reported to beat SMS-EGO, PESMO, TS-TCH and qParEGO in sequential optimization on all problems evaluated.
numbers: Wall time an order of magnitude below PESMO on CPU in sequential optimization. Problems: Branin-Currin (d=2, M=2), C2-DTLZ2 (d=12, M=2, 1 constraint), vehicle crash-safety design, video-streaming policy, DTLZ2 (d=6, M=2) with budget of 100 evaluations.
limits: TS-TCH had the fastest wall time but worse optimization. Assumes a smooth GP surrogate and little noise (noisy case in a09).
agent_relevance: Sample-efficient choice of the next probe when each evaluation is costly. For our agent an evaluation is a model call or code run.

source: Daulton, Balandat, Bakshy (2021) Parallel Bayesian Optimization of Multiple Noisy Objectives with Expected Hypervolume Improvement
finding: qNEHVI extends qEHVI to noisy observations by integrating over uncertainty in the Pareto frontier. It is one-step Bayes-optimal for hypervolume in noisy and noiseless settings and is reported to be substantially more robust to noise than earlier multi-objective BO.
numbers: qNEHVI achieves the greatest hypervolume for increasingly large batch sizes on most benchmarks; sequential qNEHVI-1 had the lowest GPU wall time of any method tested on every experiment.
limits: Authors' own benchmarks. Wall-time details in Appendix H.
agent_relevance: Model outputs are noisy. A noise-aware selector avoids locking in a spurious Pareto point (G3, G4).

source: Mouret, Clune (2015) Illuminating search spaces by mapping elites
finding: MAP-Elites keeps the best solution in each cell of a user-chosen low-dimensional feature space. It maps how performance varies across the space and the trade-offs, rather than returning one winner. Authors argue it avoids local optima by exploring many cells at once.
numbers: Algorithm: random start genomes, then repeat: pick a random elite, mutate, place the child in its cell if the cell is empty or the child is better. Cites other work finding higher global performance than separate searches.
limits: A description and guide paper; most quantitative claims are cited from other papers. Feature dimensions are chosen by the user.
agent_relevance: Alternative to a Pareto set for S7: keep one best per niche so the candidate pool stays diverse (G4).

source: Yang et al. (2023) Large Language Models as Optimizers (OPRO)
finding: OPRO puts earlier solutions with their scores into the prompt and asks the LLM for a better one. It works on small linear regression and TSP, and on prompt optimization.
numbers: Best optimized prompts beat human-designed prompts by up to 8% on GSM8K and up to 50% on Big-Bench Hard tasks. Up to 8 instructions sampled per step.
limits: Single objective only. Not meant to beat gradient methods. Sensitive to prompt format; the optimizer often gets stuck on the same instruction for tens of steps.
agent_relevance: Score-in-prompt loops give gains when the score comes from code. Single objective, so not a trade-off method.

source: Yang et al. (2023) Large Language Models as Optimizers (OPRO)
finding: TSP results show scale limits: gpt-4 beats gpt-3.5-turbo and text-bison, but all degrade fast with size and the farthest-insertion heuristic wins at larger n.
numbers: Optimality gap % at n=15: text-bison 4.4, gpt-3.5 1.2, gpt-4 0.2 (farthest insertion 1.2). n=20: 30.4, 4.4, 1.4 (FI 0.2). n=50: 219.8, 133.0, 11.0 (FI 9.8). n=10: all LLMs 0.0. Five instances per n. gpt-4 reached the optimum about 4x faster at small n.
limits: Only 5 instances per size. text-bison never found the optimum for n>=15. Weaker LLMs stuck in local optima with up to 20x worse gaps.
agent_relevance: A plain LLM searcher decays with problem size while code heuristics keep their lead. Keep search in code; use the model as a proposal slot (G7).

source: Liu et al. (2024) Large Language Models as Evolutionary Optimizers (LMEA)
finding: LMEA asks the LLM to pick parents and write crossover and mutation children for TSP, with self-adapting temperature. It beats OPRO on all eight test sets.
numbers: Optimality gap %, LMEA vs OPRO: rue-15 0.06 vs 5.23; rue-20 3.94 vs 26.30; rue-25 18.72 vs 53.59; clu-20 4.05 vs 19.83; clu-25 10.06 vs 48.25; rue-10 0.00 both. Concorde exact solver as ground truth, 5 instances per set. Without temperature self-adaptation rue-20 gap was 11.82 vs 3.94.
limits: GPT-3.5 only. Fails to scale past about 20 nodes, where classic insertion heuristics (1 to 3 percent) win. Single objective.
agent_relevance: Population-style prompting beats history-only prompting. Raising temperature only when stuck fits doubt-only-on-signal (G1).

source: Liu et al. (2024) Large Language Model for Multi-objective Evolutionary Optimization (MOEA/D-LLM, MOEA/D-LO)
finding: First LLM as a search operator inside a decomposition-based MOEA. The multi-objective problem is split into single-objective subproblems and GPT-3.5 Turbo proposes children zero-shot. Competitive hypervolume with ordinary MOEA/D on five real-world engineering problems (RE21 to RE25).
numbers: Settings: 50 subproblems, neighbourhood 10, 1,000 max evaluations, 10 input individuals, 2 outputs. Pareto fronts largely overlap with MOEA/D, especially RE25.
limits: Compared with MOEA/D only; five problems. Authors name two issues: the LLM is a black box and its inference is far more costly than a normal operator.
agent_relevance: Decomposition into single-objective subproblems eases the LLM's job. For S7 do not ask the model for the Pareto set; ask for one better candidate under a stated weight.

source: Liu et al. (2024) Large Language Model for Multi-objective Evolutionary Optimization (MOEA/D-LLM, MOEA/D-LO)
finding: Authors fit LLM behaviour with a white-box weighted linear operator plus noise (MOEA/D-LO) needing no LLM calls. It is competitive with NSGA-II and MOEA/D on ZDT and UF test sets but not best everywhere.
numbers: Hypervolume win/loss/tie of the other method against MOEA/D-LO: NSGA-II 2/11/1, MOEA/D 3/9/2, MOEA/D-DE 7/5/2 (MOEA/D-DE better on 7 of 14). ZDT4 HV: MOEA/D-LO 0.7207, NSGA-II 0.7192, MOEA/D-DE 0.3012. UF1 HV: MOEA/D-DE 0.7201, MOEA/D-LO 0.6561, NSGA-II 0.6087. 14 instances (ZDT, UF1-UF9).
limits: Operator was derived from LLM behaviour on a few instances; tests are benchmark suites, not real design problems.
agent_relevance: What looks like LLM reasoning in a search loop can be replaced by a cheap code operator. Matches G7: pay for the model only where it beats code.

source: Yao et al. (2025) Multi-objective Evolution of Heuristic Using Large Language Model (MEoH)
finding: MEoH runs a non-dominated search over LLM-written heuristics with two objectives: solution gap and running time. A dominance-dissimilarity measure (code distance plus objective dominance) manages the population. It beat single-objective EoH and FunSearch on efficiency.
numbers: Online bin packing and TSP with GPT-3.5-turbo, 3 repeats. Up to 10x less running time at similar gap. Bin packing Weibull 5k C500: FunSearch 3.319% gap, 195.7 s; EoH 0.391%, 502.9 s; MEoH 0.080%, 59.1 s.
limits: Not uniform: for 100k C100 MEoH gap was 1.387% vs EoH 0.753% (time far smaller). Only GPT-3.5-turbo.
agent_relevance: Adding a cost objective stops always choosing the slowest best-gap answer. S7 should rank on accuracy and token cost together.

source: Liu et al. (2024) Evolution of Heuristics (EoH)
finding: EoH evolves both a thought (text idea) and code, reaching strong online bin-packing heuristics with far fewer LLM calls than FunSearch.
numbers: Fraction of excess bins improved from 0.962 to 0.993 in 20 generations with about 2,000 LLM queries; FunSearch reported about 1 million. At capacity 500 FunSearch was worse than two hand-crafted heuristics while EoH got a 2.13% gap.
limits: Single objective. FunSearch numbers partly from its own report.
agent_relevance: Evolving a short idea plus code beats evolving code only. Search budget counts in model calls.

source: Li, Xiong, Wang (2025) iDSE: Navigating Design Space Exploration in High-Level Synthesis Using LLMs
finding: First LLM-aided design space exploration for HLS. Feature-driven pruning shrinks the space, the LLM writes warm-start seed designs, then LLM refinement runs a few rounds. It beats heuristic DSE on closeness to a reference Pareto front.
numbers: ADRS geometric-mean improvement: 16.6x over NSGA-II, 12.7x ACO, 9.9x MOEA/D, 15.3x Lattice, 5.1x HGBO-DSE over 12 benchmarks (PolyBench, MachSuite, CHStone). Under 50 explored designs. Matches NSGA-II (about 108 designs) with 4.6% of the designs.
limits: Reference front built by sampling, not proven optimal (exhaustive only for stencil2d, autocorr, sha). Baselines averaged over 5 runs; LLM warm start over 5 DeepSeek-R1 calls. Lattice won autocorr.
agent_relevance: The LLM's value is in the first batch: a knowledge-informed seed set beats random start. Use the model to propose diverse initial candidates; code selects.

source: Li, Xiong, Wang (2025) iDSE: Navigating Design Space Exploration in High-Level Synthesis Using LLMs
finding: Ablation: pruning removes invalid designs, trajectory reflection adds more, domain knowledge adds most. The first LLM batch alone reached the baseline target ADRS on all benchmarks.
numbers: Invalid designs 12.4% of the baseline's; pruning (S1) removed 89.9% of invalid designs; trajectory reflection (S2) improved effectiveness 20.5%; domain-knowledge injection (S3) a further 45.0%. Budget to target ADRS: 11.0x geomean speedup over meta-heuristic DSE, 4.4x over SOTA DSE (appendix: 25.1x NSGA-II, 7.6x ACO, 7.0x MOEA/D, 11.3x Lattice, 1.7x HGBO-DSE).
limits: Gains are the authors' own. Target ADRS is set by the baseline's budget, which favours the LLM at small budget.
agent_relevance: Domain prior (S3) mattered more than reflection (S2). Revision from real output helps but encoded knowledge helps more.

source: Li, Xiong, Wang (2025) iDSE: Navigating Design Space Exploration in High-Level Synthesis Using LLMs
finding: Warm start helps classical optimizers too: Latin hypercube and beta sampling beat random start; LLM seed designs beat them. Gain was smallest for ACO.
numbers: ADRS drops substantially when seed designs approximate the reference front better. Beta sampling and LHS beat random sampling across NSGA-II, ACO and MOEA/D.
limits: Authors only guess why ACO gained little.
agent_relevance: Initial diversity matters as much as later search. Fits an agent that samples k varied attempts then selects.

source: Sharma, Fu, Haris, Cano (2026) LLM-Driven Design Space Exploration of FPGA-based Accelerators (SECDA-DSE)
finding: Early vision paper for LLM-guided accelerator design with retrieval, chain-of-thought and a feedback loop for fine-tuning. Evidence is one feasibility check.
numbers: One generated accelerator design met HLS timing and resource limits on a Zynq-7000 FPGA. No Pareto comparison.
limits: Preliminary; n=1; no baseline, no hypervolume.
agent_relevance: Weak evidence; do not cite as a measured gain. Shows hardware is where most LLM-DSE work sits.

source: Shih et al. (2025) A Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Design Space Exploration in Autonomous Driving Systems
finding: Multi-agent LLM DSE with 3D simulation and profiling tools that read visual and text run outputs. Compared with a genetic algorithm on a robotaxi application.
numbers: With 15 iterations the LLM agent found 6 design points on the Pareto front (from exhaustive search); the GA found 0. The GA first reached a Pareto point at iteration 20.
limits: One application, one budget, short run where a GA has little time. Prompting analysis cut for page limit.
agent_relevance: In the few-iteration regime LLM priors beat a GA. The edge likely fades as budget rises.

source: Xiong et al. (2026) MicroEvo: Knowledge-Guided LLM Sampling for Efficient Microarchitecture Design Space Exploration
finding: LLMs inside Monte Carlo tree search with a Pareto-aware tree policy and memory of insights. Beats NSGA-II, MOTPE, Boom-Explorer (BO), RL-DSE and LEMOE (an earlier LLM method) at 20 and 45 evaluations.
numbers: Budget 20: HV NSGA-II 0.5826, MicroEvo-Gemini 0.7936 (+36.22%), MicroEvo-DeepSeek 0.7822 (+34.27%); ADRS 0.1666 vs 0.0716. Budget 45: HV 0.663 vs 0.821 (+23.94%), ADRS 0.123 vs 0.056. At budget 20: MOTPE +3.99%, LEMOE +15.80%, Boom-Explorer +6.48%, RL-DSE +8.82%. Five trials.
limits: Gain shrinks as budget grows (36.2% to 23.9%). At budget 45 LEMOE ADRS was worse than NSGA-II (-3.87%).
agent_relevance: Best small-budget result for knowledge-guided LLM search, yet an earlier LLM method lost to plain NSGA-II on ADRS at 45 evaluations. Not every LLM search helps.

source: Wong et al. (2025) LLM2TEA: An Agentic AI Designer for Discovery with Generative Evolutionary Multitasking
finding: LLM-driven multitask evolutionary algorithm for conceptual airplane and car design, with text-to-3D generation and a physics simulator in the loop.
numbers: Hypervolume 2.74x (airplane) and 1.97x (car) versus the text-to-3D baseline; novel-design diversity up 97% to 174%; over 73% of designs better in physical performance than baseline.
limits: Baseline is a text-to-3D generator without evolutionary search, not a strong classical optimizer.
agent_relevance: Novelty and feasibility come from the simulator, not the model's opinion (G8).

source: Marler, Arora (2004) Survey of multi-objective optimization methods for engineering
finding: Surveys continuous nonlinear multi-objective methods, grouped by when the decision-maker states preferences. Bibliographic record only; full text was behind a login and was not read.
numbers: Structural and Multidisciplinary Optimization 26(6), pp. 369-395. No numbers verified.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Pointer only: use for the a priori, a posteriori and interactive taxonomy.

source: Papalambros, Wilde (Principles of Optimal Design); Deb (2001) Multi-objective optimization using evolutionary algorithms
finding: Named key works for this subfield. Not opened this session; no claim is made from them.
numbers: none
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Reading-plan entry only.
